messages:
suzanne: Thinking out loud — proposal for an observability-driven adaptive fallback for canary/A-B rollouts. Goal: automatic fallback when latency or quality regressions are detected per-tenant, but avoid noisy flip-flopping.

liam: Love the direction. What are the primary signals you want the decision to use? p95, failures, semantic drift? :thinking:

suzanne: Top-level: p95 latency, per-request decode errors, and a semantic-similarity delta on a small seeded prompt set (per-tenant). Also deployment-level throughput and queue-depth to detect saturation.

raj: We should add cost signal too — if a fallback doubles cost for a tenant we need a policy to prefer degraded performance over catastrophic spend.

olga: For Private deployments we also need an immutable audit trail for any automatic fallback (who/what triggered it) to satisfy compliance teams. Logging must be exportable to customer KMS-backed sinks.

kevin: Also think about where the decision lives. My vote: hybrid. Lightweight guard in runtime for latency and errors; control plane evaluates semantic/quality signals (needs full eval harness). Runtime can do immediate hedging for SLOs.

suzanne: Agreed. Runtime-level fast guard => latency/circuit switch. Control plane => quality regressions and longer term rollbacks. Runtime publishes event with reason codes so control plane can correlate.

liam: What about hysteresis? We should prevent oscillation when signal is noisy. Simple approach: 3-tier states (closed -> degraded -> open) with configurable hold windows + exponential backoff on re-open.

raj: +1. Also cap number of automatic cutbacks per tenant per week. Manual override must be easy.

oncall-bot: Incident note: last week auto-fallback triggered 4 times for tenant-x during load spike, caused weird client retries. We should ensure fallback reduces overall retries.

kevin: For canaries we can do two-phase fallback: 1) soft restrict (mirror traffic, mark as dark) 2) hard switch (route away). Mirroring gives control plane samples while minimizing blast radius.

olga: Mirroring in Dedicated needs careful network and cost accounting. Mirror sampling rate must be small by default (1-5%).

suzanne: Sketch of runtime config snippet (proto-ish):

```yaml
fallback_policy:
  mode: adaptive
  latency_slo_ms: 250
  quality_drop_pct: 5
  min_canary_samples: 500
  mirror_sample_pct: 2
  max_auto_cutbacks_per_week: 2
  audit_export: true
```

liam: Nice. Implementation notes: runtime should evaluate sliding-window metrics every N seconds (configurable) and emit a single compact event: `fallback_decision:{tenant,variant,reason,confidence}`. Control plane ingests and can escalate to rollout rollback.

raj: On confidence: we need a simple scoring function that weights signals and normalizes by sample size. Avoid binary triggers until min samples satisfied.

kevin: UX: make the fallback reason human-readable and include eval-hash so SREs can re-run the exact prompt set.

olga: For Private customers we may need to allow them to host the control-plane evaluator locally. Offer a lightweight local evaluator package that consumes runtime events and policy.

suzanne: Risks: 1) noisy semantic evals false-positive 2) oscillation across tenants 3) cost surprises from mirroring. Mitigations: seeded evals + per-tenant baselines, hold windows, cost caps and preflight quotas.

liam: Tests: simulate staged load with synthetic semantic drift and verify no more than one auto-cutback per 30m in steady-state. Also chaos tests for network partitions between runtime and control plane.

raj: Ops: we need dashboards for auto-fallbacks, by-tenant SLA impact, and an alert when auto-fallback rate spikes.

kevin: API surface: expose `/rollouts/{id}/fallbacks` listing decisions, and allow `POST /rollouts/{id}/override` for manual revert with audit note.

suzanne: Action items: I'll draft an RFC with control-plane <> runtime contract, sample event schema, and recommended default policy values. @kevin can you list the minimal runtime metrics we need? @olga can you capture audit/export constraints for Private?

kevin: On it.

olga: Will do, adding KMS/export notes.

raj: I'll prototype the scoring function and run a quick sim.

liam: sgtm. :thumbsup:

suzanne: Thanks everyone — aiming to share RFC draft by EOD Friday. :rocket:
